annotationMethod: Choose integer X from the visually projected pelvis or prone hip center independently of the support ROI horizontal location. Choose support-specific near sole, knee, hip-side, torso or forearm ROI; integer Y must equal its exclusive alpha>=64 maximum. Weapon bounds and lifted far boots do not define later fall roots. For each army, independently select native cap-only and near-support-sole ROIs in the four contact cells; recompute alpha>=64 cap top and exclusive sole bottom, subtract, sort the four spans and round the midpoint median half up. Apply that one unchanged contact reference to its entire contact and casualty pair. Natural lunge/crouch/fall projection is retained without individual phase-height normalization.

groundMethods: Projected pelvis X follows the hips below the coat, independently of the boot X. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the nearer viewer-left supporting boot, below its cuff; weapon pixels are excluded.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips behind the extended arms. Ground Y uses the nearer viewer-left trailing support-boot sole; the forward viewer-right foot and rifle do not define the anchor.
Projected pelvis X follows the withdrawn hips beneath the coat. Ground Y uses the nearer viewer-left support-boot sole and excludes the lower weapon extremity.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips beneath the high block. Ground Y uses the nearer viewer-left support-boot sole; rifle tip and farther boot are excluded.
Projected pelvis X follows the leaning hips below the coat. Ground Y is the alpha>=64 exclusive bottom of the nearer viewer-left support boot; the released rifle is excluded.

Projected pelvis X follows the hips above the bent legs. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the nearer bent knee/proximal shin beneath the body. The rear lifted boot, reaching hands and released rifle are excluded.
Projected pelvis X follows the collapsing hips. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the folded near knee beneath the pelvis, independently of the trailing boot and released weapon.
Projected pelvis X follows the prone hip center under the pack. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 lower edge of the near forearm/torso support, isolated from the separate rifle and boots.
Projected pelvis X follows the pants/hip center below the coat and pack, independently of the support foot. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the nearer viewer-left boot sole.

Projected pelvis X follows the hips behind the extended forearm and weighted front leg. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the viewer-left supporting boot, separate from the weapon and far boot.
Projected pelvis X follows the withdrawn hips below the rear pouch. Ground Y uses the nearer viewer-left support-boot sole below the cuff.
Projected pelvis X follows the hips beneath the raised two-hand block. Ground Y uses the nearer viewer-left support-boot sole; raised weapon bounds do not affect it.
Projected pelvis X follows the tilted hips below the rear pouch. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the nearer descending boot/toe support; the separate falling rifle is excluded.

Projected pelvis X follows the hips as the body drops. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the nearer bent knee/proximal shin, with X restricted beyond the released rifle butt; the lifted boots are excluded.

Projected pelvis X follows the rolling hip center beneath the rear pouch. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the nearer folded knee/hip-side support; the separate musket and outward boot soles are excluded.

Projected pelvis X follows the prone hip center below the rear pouch. Ground Y is the exclusive alpha>=64 bottom of the near lower-torso/forearm ground support; the separately lying musket and extended boots are excluded.
